page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Quiescence
steps.margin_note: Definition, the external cause, and how quickly it ends.
lines: QUIESCENCE is a delayed seed germination that
happens when the EXTERNAL conditions are wrong:
too dry, too warm or too cold.
Give the seed the right conditions and it
steps.why: Nothing is wrong with the seed, so correcting the surroundings is enough to start germination immediately.
common_mistakes: Saying quiescence is caused by something inside the seed. That is DORMANCY.
Leaving out the named conditions. Dry, warm or cold is what the definition specifies.

steps.label: Dormancy
steps.margin_note: Mirror the quiescence lines. The word 'innate' is the mark.

lines.text: Outside conditions cause quiescence; the seed

lines: DORMANCY is the INNATE inhibition of germination,
even when the seed is placed in the most
Its causes are inside the seed: a hard coat,
chemical inhibitors, or a need for chilling.
steps.why: The word innate is what carries the definition: the block is built into the seed, so good conditions alone cannot remove it.
common_mistakes: Defining dormancy by bad weather. Dormancy persists in the BEST conditions.
Leaving out the word innate or internal. It is what separates the two terms.
steps.memory_tip: Dormancy is the seed's own fault.
